name: St. Ita
bio: St. Ita is the early Irish saint to whom tradition attributes a lullaby to the infant Jesus, which she is said to have sung while nursing him in her cell. George Sigerson, in Bards of the Gael and Gall (1907), dates her 480–570 and prints the poem under the title “Jesukin”.

The Irish original is preserved in the commentary to the Martyrology of Oengus, which Sigerson cites through Whitley Stokes. Only Sigerson’s version, made after the metre of the original, is given here.

poems.title: Jesukin
poems.author: St. Ita
poems.collection: Bards of the Gael and Gall (1907)
poems.text:
Lives my little cell within;
What were wealth of cleric high —
All is lie but Jesukin.

Nursling nurtured, as 'tis right —
Harbours here no servile sprite —
Jesu of the skies, who art
Next my heart thro' every night!

Jesukin, my good for aye,
Calling and will not have nay,
King of all things, ever true,
He shall rue who will away.

Jesu, more than angels aid,
Fosterling nor formed to fade,
Nursed by me in desert wild,
Jesu, child of Judah's Maid.

Sons of Kings and kingly kin,
To my land may enter in;
Guest of none I hope to be,
Save of Thee, my Jesukin!

Unto heaven's High King confest
Sing a chorus, maidens blest!
He is o'er us, though within
Jesukin is on my breast!
